birth-relative timing is not expressible, so the measurement year is used (late-December births may be dosed in the following year and would wrongly appear unmet)\"}}","exclusions":"[]"}],"coverage_notes":["The 'within 1 week of birth' timing is not representable with measurement-year windows; the numerator only checks for any nirsevimab dose in the measurement year (declared as derived, needs human review).","Infants born April–September: 1 dose nirsevimab 'shortly before start of RSV season' — not encoded as a rule because timing depends on local RSV season onset and maternal RSV vaccination status (both uncomputable).","Mother received RSV vaccine at least 14 days prior to delivery: nirsevimab not needed but can be considered at provider discretion — not a rule (clinician judgment); such infants are excluded from the denominator only via the uncomputable maternal-status criteria.","Infants with prolonged birth hospitalization (e.g., prematurity) discharged October through March should be immunized shortly before or promptly after discharge — not encoded (hospitalization/discharge timing not representable).","Special situations, second RSV season, ages 8–19 months: chronic lung disease of prematurity requiring medical support in the 6 months before the second season, severe immunocompromise, cystic fibrosis with weight-for-length <10th percentile or severe lung disease, and American Indian or Alaska Native children — 1 dose nirsevimab shortly before second season; not encoded (ages in months, season-relative timing, clinical severity criteria and race/ethnicity not reliably computable).","Age-eligible children undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass: 1 additional dose nirsevimab after surgery — not encoded (surgery-relative timing, dosing per FDA label).","Seasonality note: administration recommended October through March (optimally October–November or within 1 week of birth); jurisdictions with different RSV seasonality (e.g., Alaska, tropical climates) should follow local public health guidance — jurisdiction logic not representable.","Palivizumab interaction: nirsevimab can be given to palivizumab-eligible children; children who received nirsevimab should not receive palivizumab for the same season — product-choice/contraindication logic not encoded.","Maternal RSV vaccination (Abrysvo): 1 dose for pregnant persons at 32 weeks 0 days through 36 weeks 6 days gestation from September through January — not encoded as a rule because the text states either maternal vaccination or infant nirsevimab is recommended (alternative strategies, so neither is independently required), and gestational age/seasonal timing are not reliably in structured data; no vocabulary concept exists for maternal RSV vaccine.","Not recommended (listed, not rules): RSV vaccine for all other pregnant women; additional RSV vaccine doses in subsequent pregnancies. Infants born to women vaccinated in a previous pregnancy should receive nirsevimab — folded into the infant rule's maternal-status uncomputable criterion.","Dosing (weight-based dose amounts) and product choice are not in this section's representable content and are not encoded."]}
